name: AWS API Gateway
description: Protects against destructive AWS API Gateway CLI operations for both \ REST APIs and HTTP APIs.

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-rest-api
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-rest-api permanently removes a REST API and all its resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a REST API removes all resources, methods, stages, deployments, and \ configurations. All clients will immediately receive errors. API keys and usage \ plans referencing this API become orphaned but are not automatically deleted.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-rest-api: Review API details before deletion \ - aws apigateway get-stages: Check active stages and traffic \ - Export API definition with aws apigateway get-export first

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-resource
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-resource removes an API resource and its methods.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a resource removes the URL path and all HTTP methods defined on it. \ Clients calling that endpoint will receive 404 errors. Child resources are \ also deleted recursively.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-resources: Review resource tree first \ - Deploy to a test stage to verify the change \ - Delete individual methods instead if only removing specific operations

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-method
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-method removes an HTTP method from a resource.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a method removes the HTTP operation (GET, POST, etc.) from a resource. \ Clients calling that method will receive 404 or 405 errors after redeployment.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-method: Review method configuration first \ - Test changes in a non-production stage \ - Consider disabling the method instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-stage
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-stage removes a deployment stage from an API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a stage stops all traffic to that deployment. Stage variables, \ caching settings, and throttling configurations are lost. Clients using \ the stage URL will receive errors immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-stage: Review stage settings first \ - Redirect traffic to another stage before deletion \ - Export stage configuration for backup

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-deployment
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-deployment removes a deployment from an API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a deployment removes a specific API snapshot. If the deployment is \ currently active on a stage, that stage becomes unavailable. Rollback to this \ version becomes impossible after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-deployments: List deployments first \ - Ensure no stages reference this deployment \ - Keep recent deployments for rollback capability

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-api-key
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-api-key removes an API key.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an API key immediately revokes access for any client using that key. \ Requests will be rejected with 403 Forbidden. Usage tracking history for the \ key is preserved but the key cannot be recovered.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-api-key: Review key details first \ - Disable the key instead of deleting to preserve for audit \ - Notify affected clients before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-authorizer
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-authorizer removes an authorizer from an API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an authorizer breaks authentication for all methods using it. Those \ methods will fail authorization until reconfigured. Lambda authorizer functions \ are not deleted but become orphaned.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-authorizers: Review authorizers first \ - Update methods to use a different authorizer before deletion \ - Test in a non-production stage first

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-model
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-model removes a model from an API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a model removes the JSON schema definition. Methods referencing this \ model for request/response validation will lose that validation. The API will \ still function but without schema enforcement.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-models: Review models first \ - Check which methods reference this model \ - Update method configurations to remove model references first

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-domain-name
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-domain-name removes a custom domain name.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a custom domain name breaks all traffic using that domain. The ACM \ certificate is not deleted but becomes unused. DNS records pointing to the \ domain will fail to resolve API traffic.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-domain-names: Review domains first \ - Update DNS records before domain deletion \ - Verify no production traffic uses this domain

destructive_patterns.name: apigateway-delete-usage-plan
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigateway delete-usage-plan removes a usage plan.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a usage plan removes throttling and quota limits for associated API \ keys. Keys lose their rate limiting, which may cause backend overload or \ unexpected billing. Key associations are removed.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigateway get-usage-plans: Review plans first \ - aws apigateway get-usage-plan-keys: Check associated keys \ - Migrate keys to another plan before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-api
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-api permanently removes an HTTP API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an HTTP API removes all routes, integrations, stages, and configurations. \ All clients will immediately lose access. WebSocket connections are terminated. \ The API ID cannot be reused.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-api: Review API details first \ - aws apigatewayv2 export-api: Export OpenAPI spec for backup \ - Verify no production traffic before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-route
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-route removes a route from an HTTP API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a route removes the path and method combination from the API. Clients \ calling that endpoint will receive 404 errors. Route authorization settings \ and request validation are also removed.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-routes: List routes first \ - Test in $default stage before production \ - Consider updating the route instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-integration
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-integration removes an integration from an HTTP API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an integration breaks routes using it. Those routes will fail to \ invoke backend services. Lambda function configurations, HTTP endpoints, \ and VPC link settings are lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-integrations: Review integrations first \ - Check which routes use this integration \ - Update routes to use a different integration first

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-stage
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-stage removes a stage from an HTTP API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a stage stops all traffic to that deployment. Stage variables, access \ logs, throttling, and auto-deploy settings are lost. Clients using the stage \ URL will receive errors.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-stages: Review stages first \ - Redirect traffic before deletion \ - Keep $default stage for production traffic

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-authorizer
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-authorizer removes an authorizer from an HTTP API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an authorizer breaks authentication for routes using it. JWT validation \ and Lambda authorization will fail. Routes must be updated to remove or replace \ the authorizer reference.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-authorizers: Review authorizers first \ - Update routes to use a different authorizer \ - Test authorization changes in a test stage

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-domain-name
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-domain-name removes a custom domain name from an HTTP API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a custom domain breaks traffic using that hostname. API mappings are \ removed. DNS records will fail to route to the API. The ACM certificate \ remains but becomes unused.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-domain-names: Review domains first \ - Update DNS before deletion \ - Remove API mappings first to verify impact

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-route-response
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-route-response removes a route response from an HTTP API.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a route response removes response configuration for WebSocket APIs. \ Response selection expressions and model mappings are lost. Clients may \ receive unexpected response formats.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-route-responses: Review responses first \ - Test in a non-production stage \ - Update response instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: apigatewayv2-delete-integration-response
destructive_patterns.description: aws apigatewayv2 delete-integration-response removes an integration response.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an integration response removes response mapping for WebSocket APIs. \ Template transformations and response codes are lost. Clients may receive \ raw backend responses.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws apigatewayv2 get-integration-responses: Review first \ - Test response handling in a test stage \ - Update the response instead of deleting
